opening.headline: To find documents with the same meaning even if the keywords are different, embedding and vector search are needed, which convert the text into a numeric vector and compare it by distance.
body: A user searches for "How do I get a refund?", but if the title of the required document is Payment Cancellation and Payment Return Procedures, the keyword search misses this document. The two sentences have few overlapping words, but their meaning is the same. To find documents with the same meaning, you need a way to compare meaning, not text.

In this class, we will look at what embedding is, which turns text into a list of numbers with meaning, and how vector search, which measures similarity by the distance between vectors, works. Next, we compare the embedding models of OpenAI, Gemini, and Voyage AI on two axes: dimension and task type, and provide commentary on cases of reducing dimensionality when storage costs increase and cases of reading calls that do not match the task type.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the meaning of embedding, dimensionality, similarity, and vector search
Distinguish how task types and dimensions impact search quality and cost

screens.title: It means the same thing, but the keywords are different so I can't find it.
screens.lead: First, read the footage from the user who entered your question in the search bar. I read this while thinking about why the document I want is not appearing in the search results.

visual.alt: A scene where keyword search results are empty because the words in the search term and the document title do not overlap, and a scene where semantic search finds the document.
labels: How do I get a refund?

paragraphs: In the customer center search bar, the user entered “How do I get a refund?” There are definitely documents required. This document is titled Payment Cancellation and Money Return Procedure. However, the keyword search results are empty.

The reason is simple. Keyword search looks at whether the same words exist in the query and document. Refund, payment cancellation, and payment return have the same meaning, but because the letters are different, these two sentences, which have almost no overlapping words, are treated as different content.

To find documents with the same meaning, you need to compare the meaning, not the letters. So how can we convert the meaning into a form that a computer can compare? The question we will cover in this class is how to convert meaning into numbers and compare them.

callout.label: question of the day
callout.text: How can we convert meaning into numbers and compare them?

screens.outro: First, let's think about where we found the cause of our poor search quality experience.

screens.title: Reasons for poor search quality
screens.lead: Where did you find the cause of your experience with poor search quality? When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Which was the problem: query expression, document splitting, or model selection?
items.answer: When a search does not work well, the cause does not lie in one place. The user's query expression may have been different from the document, the way the document was divided may have been awkward, or the model that converts meaning into numbers may not have fit the purpose. When you identify where the problem is, you can see where to fix it.

items.prompt: Has there ever been a time when a document with the same meaning was not nominated at all?
items.answer: Documents that are not shortlisted cannot be saved no matter how well you rank them. In these cases, the first step in comparing documents and queries is usually missed: how to express meaning. The embeddings in this lesson cover that first step.

items.prompt: What does it take to isolate the cause?
items.answer: To isolate the cause, you need to be able to verbalize how each factor affects search results. Knowing what you can control, such as the dimensions of the embedding and the type of operation, allows you to decide what to change when problems arise.

screens.outro: As a tool to isolate the cause, let's now check what embedding is.

screens.title: Embedding: Meaning as Coordinates
screens.lead: The following flashcards illustrate five concepts needed to understand embeddings. When you select a card, it flips over. Select the right arrow to go to the next card.

visual.alt: A picture where three sentences are placed as points on a two-dimensional coordinate plane, and two sentences with similar meanings are gathered close together.
labels: How do I get a refund?

cards.back: An embedding is turning text into a list of floating point numbers, or vectors. This list of numbers contains the meaning of the sentence. The key point is that sentences with different letters are created to have similar lists of numbers if they have similar meanings.

The length of a vector is called its dimension. One sentence may be expressed with hundreds of numbers or more. The longer the dimension, the richer the information that can be expressed, but the larger the number that must be stored.

The distance between two vectors indicates the relatedness of the two texts. The closer the distance, the higher the relevance, and the farther the distance, the lower the relevance. It's easy to understand if you imagine a point on a coordinate plane. Sentences with similar meanings are grouped nearby.

OpenAI's embedding fees are billed based on the number of tokens in the input. Since the output is a list of numbers, the input length is the cost. As there are more documents, both embedding and storage costs increase.

Embeddings are used not only for search, but also for clustering, recommendation, anomaly detection, and classification. The same thing is that they all use the distance between texts. This lesson focuses on search.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the concept of coordinates, let's look at the flow of vector search using this distance.

screens.title: Flow of similarity and vector search
screens.lead: The following steps show how vector search goes from document preparation to results delivery. Select the right arrow to go through the steps one by one.

visual.alt: Five-column vector search flowchart consisting of document preparation phase and query phase.
labels: Divide the document into chunks and embed them

steps.title: Step 1: Divide the document into chunks and embed them
steps.body: First, divide the document to be searched into pieces of appropriate size, or chunks. Then, we put each chunk into an embedding model to turn it into a vector. This work is done in advance before the query comes in.

steps.title: Step 2: Save to vector index
steps.body: Save the created vector in the vector index. Managed services like Databricks AI Search allow you to create indexes on source tables and find the most similar vectors using a REST API.

steps.title: Step 3: Embedding the query diagram
steps.body: When a user enters a query, the query is converted into a vector using the same model as the document. This is because the distance between the query and the document can be compared only when they are located in the same coordinate space.

steps.title: Step 4: Find nearby vectors
steps.body: Find document vectors that are close to the query vector in the index. At this time, the value that indicates how close the two vectors are is the similarity. The closer it is, the higher the similarity.

steps.title: Step 5: Pass results to model
steps.body: The chunks found are passed to the generative model and used as the basis for the answer. This is the basic flow of vector search, with the document preparation step being executed in advance and the query step being executed for each request.

steps.title: Keyword similarity and semantic similarity
steps.body: Consider the query, “When did we go to the moon?” The sentence describing the moon landing has 0% keyword similarity, but has the highest semantic similarity. Conversely, an odd mooncake sentence may have higher keyword similarity but lower semantic similarity. Semantic search is an example where it is revealed that meaning, not letters, are compared.

steps.title: Hybrid Search
steps.body: Keyword search is strong for exact term matching, and semantic search is strong for matching meanings of different expressions. Therefore, a hybrid search that uses both methods together is sometimes used. Vector search does not completely replace keyword search.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the search structure, let's compare the factors that determine quality and cost in the documents of the three providers.

screens.title: View the three companies' embedding documents side by side: models, dimensions, and task types.
screens.lead: Select each tab to compare embedding models from the OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude series in order of model name, dimension, and task type.

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body:
**Model**: There are two types: `text-embedding-3-small` and `text-embedding-3-large`. The input length limit is 8192 for both.

**Dimension**: The default vector length is 1536 for `text-embedding-3-small` and 3072 for `text-embedding-3-large`. To reduce the length without losing concept expressiveness, specify the `dimensions` parameter.

**Task Type**: A structure that uses the same model for multiple purposes without specifying a separate task type. Fees are billed based on the number of input tokens.

tabs.label: Gemini
tabs.body:
**Model**: `gemini-embedding-2` is a multimodal model that contains text, images, video, audio, and documents in one embedding space. `gemini-embedding-001` is still available for text-only purposes.

**Operation Type**: `gemini-embedding-2` indicates the operation in the form of a prefix placed before the input. Use the format `task: search result | query: {content}` for search queries and `title: {title} | text: {content}` for documents. If there is no title, write `title: none`. `gemini-embedding-001` specifies `task_type` in the call `embedContent`.

tabs.label: Claude(Voyage)
tabs.body:
**Model**: Anthropic does not provide its own embedding model, but rather directs Voyage AI to suppliers with a variety of models. There are `voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4`, `voyage-4-lite` as general-purpose models, and there is also `voyage-code-4` for codes.

**Dimension**: The `voyage-4` series is the default 1024 dimension, and also supports 256, 512, and 2048 dimensions. The input length limit is 32,000.

**Selection criteria**: If you prioritize quality, look at large, if you want balance, look at the basic type, and if you prioritize delay and cost, look at lite.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed that the choices are different for each model, we will explain the impact of each choice on cost with application examples.

screens.title: Case Commentary: Reducing Dimensions When Storage Costs Skyrocket
screens.lead: The instructor explains step by step how storage costs increase as the number of documents increases. Select the right arrow to follow the steps from reading the cause to reducing it and evaluating it.

visual.alt: Illustration of bars comparing vector length decreasing from 3072 to 256.

steps.title: situation
steps.body: As the number of documents increases, vector storage costs and retrieval delays increase. The current call is `client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-large", input=texts)`, which produces 3072 numbers per document.

steps.title: Step 1: Read the cause
steps.body: Storage amount is the number of documents multiplied by the number of dimensions and bytes per number. Since the number of documents cannot be reduced, the dimension of 3072 is a major cost. Consider whether this level of expressive power is needed for all purposes.

steps.title: Step 2: Reduce to dimensions
steps.body: The most recommended way is to specify the length at creation time. Call it like `client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-large", input=texts, dimensions=256)`. The concept representation is maintained, but its length is reduced. According to the document, in the MTEB benchmark, shortening `text-embedding-3-large` to 256 gave better results than `text-embedding-ada-002` with length 1536.

steps.title: Step 3: When reducing already created vectors
steps.body: Vectors that have already been saved must be cut manually. Leave only the first part as `shortened = emb[:256]` and normalize it to `normalized = shortened / norm(shortened)`. When cutting directly, you must re-normalize. Subtracting normalization means calculating similarity with vectors of different lengths.

steps.title: Step 4: Quantization
steps.body: Another way to reduce storage size is quantization. In Azure AI Search, int8 scalar quantization reduces index size by approximately a quarter, and binary quantization by up to 28 times. To compensate for the loss, oversampling and rescoring can be added.

steps.title: Step 5: Re-evaluate
steps.body: After reducing, we re-evaluate the search results using the same query to see how much quality has decreased. Even if your goal is to reduce costs, you won't know what you've gained or lost if you don't check quality.

screens.outro: In addition to dimensions, task type also affects quality, and this time we will read calls with mismatched task types.

screens.title: Read calls with mismatched task types
screens.lead: Selecting the highlighted verses in the two calls below will reveal the reason for the deviation and the correct format. Select the verses one by one.

data.text:
Call A query: task: search result | query: refund policy
Called Document A: task: search result | query: Request for refund within 14 days
Called Query B: task: sentence similarity | query: refund policy

marks.span: task: search result | query: Request for refund within 14 days
marks.note: The document also uses a query prefix, so the difference in roles between the query and the document is not reflected. The document is titled: Refund Information | text: Refund is embedded within 14 days. If there is no title, use title: none.

marks.span: Call A query: task: search result | query: refund policy
marks.note: This line is correct. Search queries are prefixed with task: search result. If the query and the document have different roles, use an asymmetric format and add the operation prefix only to the query.

marks.span: task: sentence similarity | query: refund policy
marks.note: This type is intended to compare similar sentences and is not intended to be used for searches or information retrieval. Search queries should be prefixed with task: search result.

screens.outro: We conclude by explaining what dimensions and task types each do.

screens.title: Key points and reflection
screens.lead: Review the key points of this lesson on one screen. Read the paragraph below and proceed to the summary screen.

paragraphs: Embedding is a method of converting the meaning of text into numeric vectors, that is, coordinates. The closer the distance between two vectors, the closer they are, and vector search finds a vector in the index that is close to the query vector. The document preparation phase occurs in advance and the inquiry phase occurs per request.

Dimensionality strikes a balance between expressiveness and storage cost, while operation type adapts the quality of the same model to its intended use. Reducing the dimension will lower the cost, but you must re-evaluate the same query to check for any decrease in quality. If accurate term matching is important, hybrid search using keyword search is also an option, and it is important to make a habit of checking any choice through evaluation.

glossary.def: Text, images, etc. are converted into numeric vectors that contain meaning.
The length of the vector. Bigger ones are more expressive, but require more storage space and more computation.
A value that indicates how close the two vectors are. The closer they are, the more similar the meaning.
This is a search that finds a vector close to the query vector in the vector index.
This is a setting that adjusts the quality by informing the embedding model of uses such as search, classification, and clustering.
This is a technique to reduce the storage size by lowering the precision of vector numbers.

misconceptions.fact: Larger dimensions increase storage costs and delays. In some cases, quality is maintained even if text-embedding-3-large is reduced to 256 dimensions, so this should be confirmed through evaluation.

misconceptions.myth: The embedding model is provided directly by all three providers.
misconceptions.fact: Anthropic does not provide its own embedding model, but refers to external providers such as Voyage AI. OpenAI and Gemini provide their own embedding models.

misconceptions.myth: Vector search completely replaces keyword search.
misconceptions.fact: Keyword search is powerful for exact term matching. Therefore, a hybrid search that uses keyword search and semantic search together is sometimes used.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Embedding changes the meaning of text into coordinates.
Vector search involves finding a vector that is close to the query vector.
Reducing the dimension reduces storage costs, but requires quality assurance.
The task type adjusts the quality of the same model to its intended use.
